1 Modelling comparison Model A vs Model B for the same task-tracking problem.

Compare the same client problem in two storage models

The task system has not changed. What changes here is the way the data is shaped and maintained.

Use this page to decide what each model makes easier, what it makes harder, and why the trade-offs matter.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
RedundancyThe same data being stored in multiple places.
Embedded dataRelated information stored directly inside one document.
Reference by IDLinking one structure to another using identifiers.
Update difficultyHow awkward it is to keep related data consistent over time.

Model A: separate-file reference pattern

records.json
[
  { "record_id": 1, "owner_id": 2, "status": "open" }
]

owners.json
[
  { "owner_id": 2, "display_name": "Sam" }
]
Separate files

This keeps owner data in one place, more like the relational habit.

owner_id

The link still exists, but code has to match the ids later.

Model B: embedded-data pattern

[
  {
    "record_id": 1,
    "owner": {
      "owner_id": 2,
      "display_name": "Sam"
    },
    "status": "open"
  }
]
Embedded owner object

This can make one read simpler, but repeated owner data can drift later.

Nested structure

One document contains more of the story, but updates may become heavier.

Trade-off table

Decision pointReference patternEmbedded pattern
RedundancyLower duplication of related dataHigher risk of duplicated nested data
Read convenienceMay require joining logic in PythonOne document can contain more of what the UI needs
Update difficultyClear source of truth for related dataRepeated nested data can become inconsistent
FlexibilityMore structured and explicitCan feel faster to change early on

Decision for this HL build

  • Keep the frontend aligned with the SQL version so the comparison stays fair.
  • Use separate JSON files with ids for users and tasks.
  • Reserve the embedded tags idea for the later algorithm extension where it becomes meaningful.

What should be clear before the parallel JSON build

  • The class can compare separate-ID models with embedded-document models using real trade-offs.
  • Redundancy and update difficulty are both visible in the comparison.
  • The move into the JSON implementation track is now based on reasoning rather than guesswork.
